foreignObject.div: Figure 6. Two oracles over identical programs, so the gap between them is the transform tier and nothing else. The same detector that finds 3.0× more structure in Tabler's icons than REPEAT can express — 11.7% against 4.0%, in 180 of 300 icons — finds none at all in QuickDraw: 0.00% of bytes, in 0 of 300 programs. Tabler's orbits are 71% quarter and three-quarter turns, which is what icons are — arrows, gears, clock faces — and not what a detector firing on noise would look like, since that would spread evenly over the eight elements. The null is what licenses the constructed corpus's 40.7%: it establishes that every fold on offer is structure the generator put there rather than structure the corpus already had. The control is visible to both oracles, which is the check that neither is blind.
